interviewQA.answer: Starting from GC roots, it marks every reachable object and sweeps everything unmarked; an isolated cycle unreachable from roots is cleanly collected.

interviewQA.question: Name three common causes of memory leaks in Single Page Applications.
interviewQA.answer: Unremoved window event listeners, active setInterval timers after route unmount, detached DOM references held in closures, and unbounded global Map caches.

sections.title: Functional Programming, Patterns & Immutability
sections.description: Apply pure functions, composition, memoization, debounce/throttle, and predictable state architecture in vanilla JavaScript.

lessons.title: Pure Functions, Immutability & ES2023 Copy-by-Value Methods
lessons.summary: A pure function always returns the same output for the same inputs and causes zero observable side effects (no global mutations, network calls, or in-place array edits).
explanation: A pure function always returns the same output for the same inputs and causes zero observable side effects (no global mutations, network calls, or in-place array edits).

ES2023 introduced non-mutating array counterparts—toSorted(), toReversed(), toSpliced(), and with(index, value)—making immutable state updates clean and fast without accidentally mutating shared arrays.
Keep business calculations (quiz scoring, progress math, filtering) in pure functions so they are trivially unit-testable.

codeExample.title: Immutable Array Updates with ES2023 Methods

keyPoints: Array.prototype.sort() mutates in place; Array.prototype.toSorted() returns a fresh sorted array.
Pure functions are deterministic, cacheable, and trivial to test with node:test.
Immutability eliminates spooky action-at-a-distance bugs in shared application state.

commonMistakes.mistake: Calling scores.sort() directly on a state array in React or a shared store
commonMistakes.fix: Use scores.toSorted() (or [...scores].sort()) so original state references remain unmutated.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting a numeric comparator in sort/toSorted (default sorts lexicographically: 10 before 2)
commonMistakes.fix: Always pass (a, b) => a - b for numeric sorting.

interviewQA.question: Why does [10, 2, 1].toSorted() return [1, 10, 2]?
interviewQA.answer: Without a compareFn, JavaScript converts elements to UTF-16 strings and sorts alphabetically ("10" < "2").

interviewQA.question: What makes a function "pure" and why do senior engineers isolate pure logic?
interviewQA.answer: Same inputs always yield the same output with zero external side effects, enabling reliable memoization, concurrency safety, and fast deterministic unit tests.

lessons.title: Debounce, Throttle & Rate-Limiting Utilities
lessons.summary: Debounce waits until a burst of events stops for N milliseconds before executing once (ideal for search inputs), while throttle guarantees execution at most once every N milliseconds during continuous events (ideal for scroll/resize analytics).
explanation: Debounce waits until a burst of events stops for N milliseconds before executing once (ideal for search inputs), while throttle guarantees execution at most once every N milliseconds during continuous events (ideal for scroll/resize analytics).
Both utilities rely on closures to hold a timer ID or timestamp across calls, and production versions expose a .cancel() method so pending timers can be cleared on unmount.
Be ready to write both debounce and throttle cleanly from scratch on a whiteboard—they are among the top 5 JavaScript frontend interview coding questions.

codeExample.title: Production Debounce with Cancellation Support

keyPoints: Debounce resets its timer on every call and fires once activity pauses.
Throttle enforces a steady maximum invocation cadence during continuous streams.
Expose .cancel() on debounced functions so pending callbacks never fire after navigation.

commonMistakes.mistake: Confusing debounce and throttle on a live scroll progress bar
commonMistakes.fix: Debounce won’t update until scrolling stops completely; use throttle (or rAF) for smooth ongoing updates.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to forward arguments (...args) and this context inside wrapper utilities
commonMistakes.fix: Capture ...args cleanly so event objects or query strings reach the wrapped function intact.

interviewQA.question: Explain the difference between debounce and throttle with one real example each.
interviewQA.answer: Debounce delays execution until calls pause for X ms (e.g., search autocomplete API calls). Throttle runs at most once per X ms window during sustained triggers (e.g., button spam protection or mousemove telemetry).

interviewQA.question: Why is a .cancel() method valuable on a debounced function?
interviewQA.answer: If a user navigates away 50ms after typing, canceling prevents a stale callback from firing against an unmounted view.

lessons.title: Function Composition, Currying & Memoization
lessons.summary: Function composition chains small single-purpose transformations (pipe(trim, toLower, slugify)) into readable data pipelines, while memoization caches pure function results by input key.
explanation: Function composition chains small single-purpose transformations (pipe(trim, toLower, slugify)) into readable data pipelines, while memoization caches pure function results by input key.
Currying transforms f(a, b) into a => b => f(a, b), enabling clean partial application such as filterByLevel("Advanced") without repeating boilerplate lambdas.
Bound memoization caches (e.g., LRU eviction or WeakMap keys) so long-lived single-page apps never leak unbounded memory.

codeExample.title: Clean pipe() & Bounded Memoization

keyPoints: pipe() applies functions left-to-right; compose() applies right-to-left.
Memoization only works safely on pure functions whose output depends solely on arguments.
Use Map with a max-size eviction or WeakMap for object arguments to avoid cache memory leaks.

commonMistakes.mistake: Memoizing an impure function that reads Date.now() or Math.random()
commonMistakes.fix: Caching impure outputs returns stale incorrect results on subsequent calls.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using unbounded plain objects as memoization caches in a server process
commonMistakes.fix: Unbounded caches grow forever until OOM; enforce a max entry count (LRU) or TTL.

interviewQA.question: What is the difference between currying and partial application?
interviewQA.answer: Currying converts an N-argument function into a sequence of N single-argument functions; partial application fixes some arguments upfront and returns a function taking the remaining ones.

interviewQA.question: When can memoization hurt performance instead of helping?
interviewQA.answer: When inputs rarely repeat (low cache hit rate) or serialization overhead of cache keys costs more than recomputing a cheap function.

lessons.title: Pub/Sub Event Bus & Observable State Architecture
lessons.summary: Decoupled frontend architectures communicate through typed Pub/Sub channels or unidirectional state stores (state + action -> newState -> notify subscribers) instead of tangled direct DOM dependencies.
explanation: Decoupled frontend architectures communicate through typed Pub/Sub channels or unidirectional state stores (state + action -> newState -> notify subscribers) instead of tangled direct DOM dependencies.
Browsers even include a native EventTarget class you can instantiate directly (`new EventTarget()`) to emit CustomEvents with built-in AbortController unsubscription support.
Always return an unsubscribe function from subscribe() so listeners detach cleanly and never pile up across re-renders.

codeExample.title: Minimal Reactive Store with Unsubscribe Teardown

keyPoints: Using a Set for listeners prevents duplicate subscriptions and supports O(1) deletion.
Returning an unsubscribe thunk from subscribe() makes cleanup ergonomic and leak-free.
Unidirectional updates make debugging and time-travel inspection straightforward.

commonMistakes.mistake: Mutating state properties in place without calling setState()
commonMistakes.fix: Direct mutations bypass subscriber notifications, leaving the UI out of sync.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to store and call the unsubscribe callback when a view unmounts
commonMistakes.fix: Zombie subscribers keep executing on removed views and leak memory.

interviewQA.question: Why is a Set better than an Array for storing Pub/Sub subscriber callbacks?
interviewQA.answer: Set automatically deduplicates identical listeners and removes callbacks in O(1) time via listeners.delete(fn) without index shifting.

interviewQA.question: What native browser class can act as a lightweight zero-dependency event bus?
interviewQA.answer: EventTarget—any class can extend EventTarget and dispatch CustomEvent instances with standard addEventListener/removeEventListener support.

sections.title: Security, Testing & V8 Engine Performance
sections.description: Defend against XSS and prototype pollution, write fast deterministic unit tests, and write JIT-friendly JavaScript.

lessons.title: Client-Side Security: XSS, Prototype Pollution & Sanitization
lessons.summary: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs whenever untrusted text is parsed as executable HTML/JS, while Prototype Pollution lets malicious JSON keys (__proto__, constructor.prototype) inject properties onto every object in the runtime.
explanation: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) occurs whenever untrusted text is parsed as executable HTML/JS, while Prototype Pollution lets malicious JSON keys (__proto__, constructor.prototype) inject properties onto every object in the runtime.

Defend in depth: use textContent instead of innerHTML, enforce a strict Content-Security-Policy (CSP), validate URL schemes (https:/http: only), and guard recursive object merges against __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys.
Never pass user strings into eval(), new Function(), or setTimeout(string)—they execute arbitrary code in your origin.

codeExample.title: Prototype-Pollution-Safe Deep Merge Guard

keyPoints: Use textContent (or trusted framework escaping) instead of innerHTML for user content.
Block __proto__, constructor, and prototype keys in deep merge/clone utilities.
Use Map instead of plain objects for arbitrary untrusted user-supplied keys.

commonMistakes.mistake: Rendering user-submitted markdown or comments with element.innerHTML = userInput
commonMistakes.fix: Escape HTML or sanitize with a vetted sanitizer like DOMPurify before inserting HTML.

commonMistakes.mistake: Merging raw JSON.parse(req.body) recursively into a config object without key filtering
commonMistakes.fix: An attacker sending {"__proto__": {"isAdmin": true}} can pollute Object.prototype across the entire process.

interviewQA.question: What is Prototype Pollution in JavaScript and how do you prevent it?
interviewQA.answer: It happens when unsafe recursive merge/path-setter code writes to __proto__ or constructor.prototype, altering Object.prototype globally. Prevent it by blocking forbidden keys, using Map, or freezing Object.prototype.

interviewQA.question: How does Content-Security-Policy (CSP) mitigate XSS even if an injection bug slips through?
interviewQA.answer: A strict CSP without unsafe-inline blocks unauthorized inline scripts and external script origins from executing in the browser.

lessons.title: V8 Hidden Classes, Inline Caches & JIT-Friendly Code
lessons.summary: Modern JS engines like V8 compile hot functions with TurboFan/Maglev JIT compilers using Hidden Classes (Shapes/Maps) and Inline Caches to achieve near-native property access speed.
explanation: Modern JS engines like V8 compile hot functions with TurboFan/Maglev JIT compilers using Hidden Classes (Shapes/Maps) and Inline Caches to achieve near-native property access speed.

Initializing object properties in a consistent order with consistent types creates monomorphic call sites (1 hidden class), whereas dynamically deleting properties (`delete obj.x`) or adding keys in varying orders degrades objects to slow dictionary mode.
Initialize all expected fields in constructors/factories (using null/undefined placeholders) instead of adding or deleting keys dynamically.

codeExample.title: Monomorphic Object Construction for Fast V8 Shapes

keyPoints: Objects created with identical keys in the same order share a single Hidden Class (Shape).
Monomorphic functions (receiving one consistent object shape) optimize dramatically better than megamorphic ones.
Avoid using delete on hot objects—assign null/undefined or use a Map for dynamic key deletion.

commonMistakes.mistake: Using delete obj[key] inside a high-frequency animation or parser loop
commonMistakes.fix: delete transitions V8 objects to slower hash-table dictionary mode; use Map for dynamic deletions.

commonMistakes.mistake: Prematurely micro-optimizing readable code before profiling with DevTools Performance flamegraphs
commonMistakes.fix: Always measure real bottlenecks first; algorithmic complexity (O(n²) -> O(n)) beats micro-tweaks 99% of the time.

interviewQA.question: What is a V8 Hidden Class (Shape) and why does property initialization order matter?
interviewQA.answer: V8 assigns a hidden structural descriptor mapping property names to fixed memory offsets. Creating objects with the same keys in the same order lets V8 reuse one Shape and read fields in a single pointer offset.

interviewQA.question: Why is algorithmic Big-O optimization usually more impactful than V8 micro-optimizations?
interviewQA.answer: Replacing an O(n²) nested array.find() with an O(1) Map lookup cuts 10,000 items from 100M operations to 10k—orders of magnitude larger than micro-tuning.

lessons.title: Deterministic Unit Testing, Fakes & Async Test Patterns
lessons.summary: Reliable JavaScript codebases test pure logic directly with fast unit tests (such as Node’s built-in node:test and node:assert/strict) while injecting clocks, storage adapters, and fetch dependencies cleanly.
explanation: Reliable JavaScript codebases test pure logic directly with fast unit tests (such as Node’s built-in node:test and node:assert/strict) while injecting clocks, storage adapters, and fetch dependencies cleanly.

Instead of letting tests depend on real wall-clock time or network latency, pass dependencies (now, storage, fetcher) as parameters with sensible defaults so every edge case runs deterministically in milliseconds.
Write tests around observable behavior and edge cases (empty lists, pass-mark boundary 69% vs 70%, corrupted input) rather than private implementation details.

codeExample.title: Zero-Dependency Unit Test with node:test

keyPoints: Node.js ships a built-in test runner (node:test) and strict assertions (node:assert/strict).
Dependency injection (passing clock/storage) eliminates flaky time-dependent tests.
Test boundary values explicitly (0, 69, 70, 100, empty arrays, invalid input).

commonMistakes.mistake: Writing assertions using loose assert.equal when types matter without strict mode
commonMistakes.fix: Always import node:assert/strict so === equality is enforced and "70" !== 70.

commonMistakes.mistake: Forgetting to await async assertions inside test callbacks
commonMistakes.fix: Return or await Promises in async tests so failures are never silently missed after the test finishes.

interviewQA.question: Why should pure domain logic be decoupled from DOM and UI components?
interviewQA.answer: Decoupled pure functions run in milliseconds in Node without a browser, have zero flakiness, and stay reusable across web, mobile, and server code.

interviewQA.question: What makes a test "flaky" and how do you eliminate flakiness?
interviewQA.answer: Dependence on real timers, network calls, random values, or shared mutable global state; fix it via dependency injection, isolated fixtures, and deterministic inputs.

lessons.title: Strict Mode, Tooling & Production Bundle Discipline
lessons.summary: Production JavaScript ships through strict static analysis (ESLint, TypeScript), module bundling with tree-shaking, source maps for error tracking, and code-splitting by route.
explanation: Production JavaScript ships through strict static analysis (ESLint, TypeScript), module bundling with tree-shaking, source maps for error tracking, and code-splitting by route.

Always inspect bundle composition: loading all 23 courses upfront would bloat initial startup, whereas lazy dynamic import() chunks load only the course the learner opens while keeping First Contentful Paint crisp.
Keep your critical initial JS bundle lean by code-splitting heavy libraries (PDF generators, code editors, syntax highlighters) behind lazy imports.

codeExample.title: Lazy Route / Feature Loading Pattern

keyPoints: Dynamic import() splits heavy features into separate on-demand JS chunks.
Promise.all([import(...), import(...)]) fetches parallel chunks simultaneously.
ES modules enforce strict mode automatically—catching accidental globals and silent write failures.

commonMistakes.mistake: Statically importing giant libraries (like PDF engines or chart suites) on the landing page
commonMistakes.fix: Dynamically import heavy features only when the user opens that view or clicks export.

commonMistakes.mistake: Shipping unminified development bundles or raw console.log spam to production
commonMistakes.fix: Run production builds (vite build) which minify, tree-shake dead code, and content-hash assets for caching.

interviewQA.question: How does code-splitting with dynamic import() improve Core Web Vitals?
interviewQA.answer: It shrinks the initial JS downloaded, parsed, and executed on page load—directly improving LCP, TBT, and INP.

interviewQA.question: Why do production bundlers attach content hashes (app.a3f91c.js) to built filenames?
interviewQA.answer: Content hashes allow aggressive immutable browser caching (Cache-Control: max-age=31536000) while guaranteeing instant cache busting whenever code changes.
